Very disappointing experience. I was told I was getting a 14-day free trial, but I was charged for a full month instead. I immediately contacted them by email to explain the situation and request a refund, but they never even responded.

On top of that, the app does not work as advertised. They make it seem like the service works at restaurants in general, but in my experience it only works with certain well-known fast-food chains. I tried using it at other restaurants and it simply wasn’t useful.

Between being charged unexpectedly, getting no response from customer service, and the app not delivering what I expected from the advertising, I would not recommend this service. Be careful before signing up for the “free trial.”

It didn’t give me the actual menu insight I was looking for, so I basically felt like I paid for the app and got nothing useful out of it.

I feel like I wasted my time. I’m not paying $50 a year for something I can find myself by going onto the restaurants website or in their app. If it was $10-20/y or free but limited, sure, that wouldn’t be a big deal, but only 7 days for free and $50 after is crazy. Especially when most people struggle to keep up with a diet after a couple weeks. They do yearly for that reason- they can charge more knowing you likely won’t keep up with it.
I’m sure it’s not a scam but it’s certainly greedy.

reviews.title: Good thought but menu items not accurate
reviews.text: Went to a couple of my local chain restaurants and tried to use the app to see what I should get. The app looked good and I was ready to go until I walked in and nothing they suggested was on the menu. Threw me for a loop. I like the design and the concept but it has to be accurate or it’s pointless. Stick to the core menu items and don’t do any limited time offers

reviews.title: Misleading and expensive app
reviews.text: App is $10 a month for it to mostly show you all fast food options. A person who’s truly tryna be”fit” as the app is called menu fit would try to pick places that wouldn’t have all these processed ingredients. This is misleading because it just giving people the idea eating at Wendy’s and mcds is good as long as you choose the “healthier” option from this app. When truly it’s not good for your health at all, doesn’t keep you full and nourished and becomes a bad cycle. This app does not have good intentions it’s just for money.

reviews.title: Preferences ignored making the app pointless to use
reviews.text:
I thought I would give this app a try but deleted it same day. 
My preferences are set to no seafood or turkey. 
No matter what restaurant I check out, if they have an item with some sort of seafood or turkey, those are my recommendations for my high protein meals. I even picked a place that I know for a fact does not have either option and it was still an option - A turkey wrap or a salmon salad. Which leads me to think this is AI generated food suggestions because The meal suggestions aren’t even actual menu items, they’re just vague descriptions of things you might be able to get. Ex cheeseburger bunless with fries or grilled chicken with side of rice.

reviews.title: Scummy
reviews.text: I was really disappointed with the Menu Fit app. It has you spend a lot of time answering question after question about your goals, preferences, and personal information, only to tell you at the very end that you have to purchase a subscription to use it. It feels misleading because you don’t find out until you’ve already invested your time. Not everything should require a subscription. It would have been much more transparent to mention the cost upfront before asking users to complete the entire setup process.

reviews.title: Didn’t realise you had to pay state-of-the-art away!!!
reviews.text:
I put this app on my phone about 5 days ago but as far as I could see it useable for 7 days without purchasing or subscribing. Not sure where I went wrong with the setting up but checked
My bank account today and money has been taken from
My account. I immediately went into my apps and deleted it. And cancelled whatever subscription they had me on. 
. I couldnt believe it.  These apps need to be more clear about immediate costs not annual or
Monthly costs. I really need a refund. How!?

reviews.title: Good Thought but Missing Things
reviews.text: Great concept for recommendations but there is some key things I feel like are missing. Doesn’t allow you to customize the foods that you might pick to see suggestions to make it healthier, doesn’t tell you portion sizes (several item have options for half size for full size), doesn’t give you information if food comes with sides, what to pick or if you get a side at all. I love the suggestions but wish they offered more.

reviews.title: Completely broken algorithm that’s impractical and wasteful
reviews.text: I downloaded this to help with a body recomposition diet. I selected high-protein, and the app immediately started suggesting absurd, completely impractical meals. For McDonald's, it gave a "98 Excellent" rating to ordering a Big Mac and a McDouble, plus two a-la-carte patties, telling me to throw away all the buns and vegetables. It literally wants you to sit in a parking lot eating 6 greasy beef patties out of a box. For Chipotle, it suggested a quadruple steak bowl with absolutely nothing else in it, no fajita veggies for low-calorie filler, nothing. At that point, why not just go buy a steak? The absolute peak of its broken logic was when I said I was craving eggs, and it suggested an egg dish WITHOUT THE EGGS just to hit a macro target. The app relies on a lazy, inflexible algorithm that treats fast food menu items like Tetris blocks to force the math to work. It has zero real-world flexibility, ignores sodium levels, and results in massive food waste. Save your money and just track your own macros.

reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.text:
Not as accurate as I would have hoped. It gave me an option that wasn’t on the menu at one place. Other places it didn’t seem accurate. It recommended a pasta dish with butter shrimp and a cream sauce for 700 calories (which seems very low for a big dish) vs me ordering grilled fish, vegetables, and potatoes. 

One place it said it included two biscuits. That would have been 300 calories for those alone and it did not appear it accounted for that at all because the total was 700 calories

reviews.title: Why is this a payed service
reviews.text: I’m just trying to find a calorie sufficient diet why tf do I have to pay you guys $10 a month just for menu suggestions?? At this rate I’ll just stuff my face like an obese person and pray I gain something from it cause it’s going to save me more money and time than this bs. And you have a whole dude on insta advertising it like it’s some free alternative to help improve your life asking strangers he meets in the street to use it saying “iLl PaY FoR YoUr MeAl If YoU ChOsE sOmEtHiNg HeAlThIer” To rope them into spending more later on?? What a joke! This is the exact reason why people eat unhealthy!!

I think that if I didn’t have to pay for it, then I would definitely use it! But another thing is, it automatically assumed that I was 150 lbs and gave me a slide bar on how much weight I wanted to lose, I am in fact not 150 pounds nor anything close to it so it makes me think that, for that part of the calculation, it would be off and not as accurate in helping me lose weight. Just something that they should change is all I am saying!

reviews.text: it’s the usual app where they lower you in with a very well-made app very well-made set up process to help you lose fat and gain protein very well all round made app. But then once you get done filling out all their stuff of course they want you to pay a monthly subscription instead of being the rightful advertisement that they advertise where it’s a free Health fitness app but of course no they’re just like every app they want you to pay a subscription. horrible.

I don’t mind paying for apps. But when you have to go through a ton of questions, picking your favorite restaurants, putting in your weight and goal weight, and giving an email/creating an account, and THEN they tell you that you must pay for the app to use it. That’s a no from me brother. 

Just be up front “hey this app is $35 a year, want to continue?” at the beginning or you seem super scammy. I would have purchased this but won’t be because of the scammy sign up style.

reviews.title: Non-existent customer support!!
reviews.text: I downloaded this app for the reason everyone else has. I thought the app was decent but don’t want to pay for it as I don’t eat out very often. They charged my account before I could cancel (my bad) but when trying to contact them through the app for a possible refund it said ‘mail not configured. Please configure a mail account on this device’ not sure what that means to be honest but I have email on my phone and my email is on the account. So I looked up their support email and emailed them a WEEK ago. Still no response. The account I use for my subscriptions is just for that, I don’t keep money in it until I need to pay for one, that being said it’s jammed up my Apple account so I can’t download or update anything. Even after putting money in there the charge won’t go through. So yeah, not happy at all. Don’t expect a response if you have problems.

reviews.title: Probably decent app can’t use though
reviews.text: Im sick of these companies pretending to have a free app that is helpful when you end up needing to pay for some useless monthly subscription. They ask for a review before even mentioning payment, greedy stuff. Can’t wait for an app to be released which actually cares about its users.

reviews.title: Misleading

They ask you a bunch of questions, take your personal information, build you a profile, and then get your email address…then, after all that, they to move forward you have to pay money. I was wanting a free resource that I could upgrade if I saw value in it. But now they have an account built for me and have my personal email address and I got nothing out of it.

reviews.title: No price is clear until you put in a lot of info and agree to a free trial…
reviews.text: I saw this in an online ad and thought to try it. While you can do a free trial, they aren’t upfront about what the cost will be after the free trial. I had put in a bunch of food preferences and an email before I got to the part where it tried to sign me up for the free trial, and with no info about what to expect if I agreed to that, I bounced out and decided not to use the app. Just be straightforward and let me know what the commitment is to use the app’s full features. If you’re not, I am not proceeding even with a free trial.

reviews.title: AI SCAM
reviews.text: It’s all AI based and you pay to use this, also has a lot of bugs, another useless cheecky app, made me waste 5 mins of my life

reviews.title: Great idea, but barely performs as advertised.
reviews.text: I really wanted to like MenuFit, but the app completely misses the mark for anyone serious about tracking macros accurately.  My biggest complaint is that you cannot properly customize your overall macro targets. Even worse, changing your weight goals barely seems to affect the recommended calories or macros at all. You can set drastically different goals and still receive nearly identical recommendations, which makes the personalization feel superficial and unreliable.  Another frustrating issue is that adjusting the meal-level macro targets appears to do almost nothing. The suggested meals are often nowhere near the targets you set, making it feel like the app is not even referencing its own settings when generating recommendations.  At that point, the app struggles to perform the most basic functions it advertises. The recommendations feel generic rather than personalized, especially for anyone following a high-protein, fitness-focused, or performance-based nutrition plan.  Overall, the app may work for casual users who just want general meal ideas, but for anyone serious about bodybuilding, fat loss, athletic performance, or accurate macro tracking, there are much better options available.

reviews.title: So Inaccurate
reviews.text: I explored this app for a few minutes after downloading. In those few minutes I came across several inaccuracies. 1) For one restaurant, is suggesting swapping the fries for a side salad. That sounds reasonable except that restaurant doesn’t serve fries at all. So if the app thinks it does, then that is probably impacting its macro and calorie count, making it inaccurate. 2) For another local restaurant (a Chinese restaurant) it was showing a Mexican menu and giving Mexican dish recommendations. That was completely wrong. 3) For one dish, it had it listed as 620 calories. I asked its AI feature how many calories were in that dish and it said 700. So which is it? The app isn’t internally consistent. I deleted it because in 5 minutes it proved to be very unreliable.

reviews.title: Good product/bad subscription process
reviews.text: They will tell you in three days they will remind you if you want to cancel your subscription. This is a lie. The app does what’s advertised however if you are unsure if you want the subscription, set your own reminders. Unfortunately, for me, I used Apple Pay so now I cannot download any apps until I have purchased the subscription that I do not want. All because I canceled a day late

reviews.title: If you only want fast food
reviews.text:

Unless you’re searching for a big chain or fast food place, don’t expect to find anything accurate. Most local restaurants either aren’t there at all or have incomplete menus, which defeats the whole purpose of the app.

I really wanted this to be helpful, but it just isn’t reliable. There’s no point in using a menu app if you can’t trust the menus. Definitely needs major improvement.

reviews.title: Not accurate at all!

Claims to have every restaurant in the world and give you the healthiest options for those restaurants, YES from my experience they do have every restaurant in the world… BUT EVERY SINGLE MENU ITEM IS WRONG It’s just a cheap app that uses a nice looking UI and some BS AI filtering software that pulls through items that aren’t even on the menu, I only download this app because I watch “ thewellroundedhuman” on YouTube but very very disappointed

I even talked with the CEO which seemed like he wanted to help, but then no response… The app does not deliver what is in its description. Functionality is extremely limited. reviews.title: Partially Helpful

I agree with some of the reviews here where at some restaurants, the menu is totally made up. For example, a local BBQ restaurant with a pretty simple menu in the restaurant but in this app, there were 10+ sophisticated appetizers (none of which were on the menu at the BBQ restaurant) and entrees that were not even BBQ related like a Vietnamese dish.  None of the menu items listed in this app for that BBQ restaurant were available at the restaurant. None of the menu items in the restaurant are available in this app for that restaurant name. I would just rather the app say that the restaurant is not available.

reviews.title: Life Changing But Not Perfect
reviews.text:
Updated Review:

This app used to be great and convenient. It recently got a major update and it absolutely broke the app. Unless you’re looking into the menu of a popular chain restaurant, it will be impossible to find the options you need for a local spot. The one function for the app is now completely gone. It has one job and it failed at it.

Old Review:

MenuFit is so convenient in browsing menu options that match your fitness goals. It’s really simple and easy to navigate. My only problem is that it isn’t always accurate with certain menus for niche restaurants, and it doesn’t show you the macros for the ‘top recommended’ items in select restaurants. Example: Chick Fil A recommended meals shows me the macros without needing to find them in the ‘menu’ tab, but with any local or niche location it often just shows me the recommended meals but no macros in the same page. I have to look for the items separately. Hopefully they fine tune this program. Other than that, very convenient and extremely helpful in finding new favorites. Recommended for sure!

Seems like an ideal app for Americans and Canadians, though.

reviews.title: Deceptive app clearly incorrect in caloric information
reviews.text: Honestly, the potential is there but this app clearly is wrong on their calories. For example - I chose a chick fil a order of 12 ct nuggets, medium fries and a diet lemonade in the menu fit app and cross referenced with the chick fil a app. Menu fit said it was 540 calories whereas chick fil a shows it’s actually 860. This is no small inaccuracy when it comes to weight loss. If this was a smaller chain I might understand but all of this information is readily available for them to update their app accordingly - huge oversight on their part.

It seem to go out of its way to not give you macro number data. After asking the built in AI 4 different ways it gave me the info, so it has the info. Not sure why it doesn’t display it with the recommendations, or a drop down for a cleaner look. Just subjective words is not helpful

reviews.title: Inaccurate Calorie Counts
reviews.text: I downloaded this app to try and have easy access to low calorie options at fast food places. I usually check calories on my own before ordering, but I wanted a way to shake things up and get some different ideas from what I usually order. Unfortunately, I used this app twice and the calorie counts were completely off both times. Once at Tazikis (Mediterranean cafe in the south) and once at McDonalds. Both times, the calorie counts for the meals I had selected were off by over 200 calories compared to the restaurant’s website. Both times, MenuFit advertised the meals as lower calories than they actually were. At Tazikis this was a 28% error and at McDonalds it was a 40% error. This is extremely disappointing for an app whose entire purpose is to promote healthy eating at fast food. A 200 calorie difference every time you eat at a restaurant will add up extremely quickly. I could not justify continuing to use this app (or especially to pay for the app) when both of my attempts to use it had been completely useless. I would like to see MenuFit adjust their calories to be accurate to what is published by the restaurant.

I was genuinely curious about what this app had to offer, and would have even considered paying for it, but I can’t even demo it without an in app purchase.
